_: THE HAND-KEPT HALF OF THE LANGUAGE-COVERAGE SCOREBOARD: the rails that compare a lane's numbers to a formula, and the differences the engine itself declares. Everything else the scoreboard knows comes from asking the doors or from the vendor harness's verdicts. A rail is listed here only after its items, its oracle and the lane it runs through were READ in the test file; `tools/pine_coverage/language_coverage.py build` refuses a registry whose test file, anchor, divergence row or item does not exist.
_rails: oracle `reference-formula`: the test differences the lane's column against an implementation written in the test from the formula TradingView publishes (an independent oracle, never the engine's own function). scope `every-bar`: the whole series is compared, holes included; `single-bar`: one bar only. ONLY an `every-bar` rail on an item for which TradingView's own reference publishes a formula or a reference implementation lifts the item to EXACT; every other rail is recorded on the item as a `definition rail` and proves nothing about TradingView. Vendor captures are NOT listed here: the harness is the one authority for them.

rails.reads: translatePine then interpret over 1,500 bars with holes; TradingView's pine_swma written as plain JS. The test's `same()` helper asserts na-ness and value on EVERY bar inside its loop; the `toBeGreaterThan(1400)` only guards that enough bars were finite (not a tolerance for mismatches)
the standard true-strength-index definition as plain JS; demoted to a definition rail unless the reference publishes a formula

knownDifferences.note: the bands are bounded recurrences re-seeded a fixed number of bars back; a band whose last reset is older can differ from TradingView's, which carries them from the first bar
the chart's own Parabolic SAR rules started a fixed number of bars back; the engine's own note says it is not TradingView's ta.sar, whose first bars and reversal details differ
TradingView's flags on a closed bar depend on when the viewer arrived; the engine defines them from its own clock and fetch (accepted divergence)
ishistory is an alias of isconfirmed here and three independent axes there (accepted divergence)
a request for the chart's own base period folds to the identity; TradingView's lookahead_off reads the last CLOSED bar (accepted divergence)
two stores answer how many shares traded with different numbers, by symbol and era (open divergence)
truncated division gives the remainder the sign of the dividend; TradingView's own page only warns that % on negatives may differ (suspected, unmeasured)
